s: Which Act made Central approval necessary for diversion of forest land?
x: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 made Central approval necessary for diverting forest land.

s: In which year was the National Green Tribunal Act enacted?
x: The order is Air Act 1981, EPA 1986, Public Liability Insurance Act 1991 and NGT Act 2010.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — legal basis for EIA and CRZ notifications
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — creation of the pollution control boards
x: The pollution control boards were created under the Water Act, 1974. The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is an umbrella law whose Section 3 supports EIA and CRZ notifications.

s: Under which Act was the Central Zoo Authority established in 1992?
x: The Central Zoo Authority was set up in 1992 under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

s: Which is regarded as India's first pollution-control law?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
x: The Water Act, 1974 is India's first pollution-control law; the NGT Act, 2010 is the latest in the chain.

s:
Arrange the following Acts in chronological order:
1. Forest (Conservation) Act
2. Water (P&CP) Cess Act
3. Air (P&CP) Act
4. Public Liability Insurance Act
x: Water Cess Act 1977, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, Air Act 1981 and PLI Act 1991.

s: In which year was the Biological Diversity Act enacted?
x: The Biological Diversity Act came in 2002, between the PLI Act (1991) and the NGT Act (2010).

s: For which purpose was the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 enacted?
o: Insurance cover for forest land diversion
Compensation to farmers for crop loss
Funding of State Pollution Control Boards
Relief to victims of accidents involving hazardous substances
x: The PLI Act, 1991 gives relief to people hit by accidents while handling hazardous substances.

s: On which date did the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 come into force?
x: The Water Act, India's first pollution-control law, came into force on 23 March 1974.

s: Which one of the following is the primary purpose of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
o: To regulate only the use of forest land
To protect and improve the environment and control pollution
To levy a cess on municipal water consumption
To establish a specialised environmental tribunal
x: The Act provides a framework for protecting and improving the environment and controlling pollution.

s: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 was enacted under which constitutional provision, to implement the decisions of which conference?
x: EPA 1986 rests on Article 253 (laws to implement international agreements) and gives effect to the Stockholm Conference (1972) decisions. Article 252 is the basis of the Water Act 1974, not EPA. Rio 1992 came after the Act. Article 51A(g) is a Fundamental Duty, not a law-making power.

s: Which Section of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 deals with penalties for contravention of the Act?
x: Section 15 sets penalties; Section 3(3) allows authorities to be constituted and Section 5 covers directions.

s: Under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, who has the power to regulate the location of industries?
x: The Centre's powers under the Act include regulating the location of industries, besides standards, hazardous waste and public health.

s: Under which provision was the National Ganga River Basin Authority constituted in 2009?
o: Section 5 of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
Section 16 of the Water Cess Act, 1977
x: The National Ganga River Basin Authority was an authority constituted under Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act.

s: The Environment Protection Fund, kept in the Public Account, is constituted under which Section of the EP Act, 1986?
x: The Fund is constituted under Section 16 and holds fines under the Air, Water and EP Acts; 75% goes to States/UTs and 25% to the Centre.

s: Under which Act have the Green Credit Rules been notified?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
x: Eco-Sensitive Zone notifications, the Plastic Waste Management Rules and the Green Credit Rules are all notified under the EP Act, 1986.

s: Which event led to the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
x: The Bhopal gas tragedy (1984) was the background to the EPA, popularly called umbrella legislation.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about notifications under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
o: Doon Valley (1989) barred industries burning over 24 MT of coal/fuel a day
Revdanda Creek (1989) barred industries around the creek
Revdanda Creek (1989) declared the area ecologically fragile and barred power plants
Dhanu Taluka (1991) was declared ecologically fragile with no power plants
x: Revdanda Creek barred industries around the creek; the 'ecologically fragile, no power plants' rule belongs to Dhanu Taluka (1991).

s: What does the Coastal Regulation Zone notification under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 mainly do?
o: regulates coastal stretches and prohibits ash or waste dumping
requires prior clearance for all forest diversion
x: The CRZ notification of 1991 regulates coastal stretches and prohibits ash and waste dumping in the regulated areas.

s: In which years were the EIA notification under the Environment (Protection) Act issued and revised?
x: The EIA notification was issued in 1994 and was subsequently revised in 2006; it provides for prior environmental clearance.

s: Which Section of the EP Act, 1986 empowers the Centre to issue directions, including closure of industries?
x: Section 5 provides for directions including closure; Section 3(3) is for authorities and Section 16 the EP Fund.

s: In what ratio is money in the Environment Protection Fund shared between States/UTs and the Centre?
x: The EP Fund gives 75% to States/UTs and 25% to the Centre.

s: What is the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 popularly called?
x: The EPA is umbrella legislation, coordinating authorities under the Water and Air Acts.

s: In which year were the Green Credit Rules under the EP Act notified?
x: The Green Credit Rules (2023) reward voluntary tree planting on degraded land.

s: Under the Doon Valley notification (1989), industries burning more than how much coal or fuel a day were not allowed?
x: The Doon Valley notification under the EPA barred industries burning over 24 MT of coal or fuel a day.

s: For the purpose of environmental enforcement under the Environment (Protection) Act framework, which body is identified as the enforcement body?
x: The Central Pollution Control Board is identified as the enforcement body under the Environment (Protection) Act framework.

s: The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) deals with which of the following types of pollution?
x: The CPCB deals with water pollution (under the 1974 Act) and air pollution (under the 1981 Act).

s: What is the status of the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)?
o: A constitutional body under the Ministry of Finance
A judicial body under the National Green Tribunal Act
x: The CPCB is a statutory body under MoEFCC and provides technical services to the Ministry under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

s: Which one of the following is primarily a function of the CPCB rather than an operational function of an SPCB?
o: Inspecting individual industrial plants within the State
Granting consent to individual industries in the State
Analysing samples collected for State-level enforcement
x: Coordination of SPCBs is a CPCB function. Inspection, sample analysis and granting consents to industries are among the operational functions of SPCBs.

s: Who nominates the chairperson of the CPCB and the chairperson of an SPCB, respectively?
x: The CPCB chairperson is nominated by the Central Government, while the SPCB chairperson is nominated by the concerned State Government.

s: In which year did the Department of Environment (1980) become the Ministry of Environment and Forests?
x: The Ministry of Environment and Forests was formed in 1985; it was renamed MoEFCC in 2014.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The CPCB is a statutory organization.
The CPCB functions at the central level.
The CPCB functions at the state level.
The CPCB was constituted in September 1974.
x: Option C is incorrect: the CPCB works at the national level. State Pollution Control Boards handle the State level.

s: Real-time air-quality information from the monitoring network is available through which application?
x: Real-time air-quality information is provided through the SAMEER app. SAFAR is a separate air-quality and weather forecasting system.

s: The National Clean Air Programme (2019) targets what reduction in PM10 by 2025-26 compared with 2019-20?
x: NCAP targets a 40% cut in PM10 by 2025-26 over 2019-20 and covers 130 cities in 24 States/UTs.

s: In which year was the Ministry of Environment and Forests renamed MoEFCC?
x: Department of Environment 1980, Ministry of Environment and Forests 1985, MoEFCC 2014.

s: Under which Act was the CPCB constituted in September 1974?
x: The CPCB was set up under the Water Act in 1974, before the Air Act (1981) existed.

s: The National Clean Air Programme (2019) covers how many cities?
x: NCAP covers 130 cities in 24 States/UTs.

s: Which of the following is a common requirement under both the Water Act, 1974 and the Air Act, 1981?
o: Compulsory registration under the Water Cess Act
Declaration of every industrial site as an air pollution control area
Prior consent of the concerned Board to establish and operate a polluting unit
Prior approval of the National Green Tribunal for every industrial unit
x: Both Acts require prior consent of the Pollution Control Board for establishing and operating a unit that may cause pollution.

s: Which one of the following was specifically added to the definition of ‘air pollutant’ by the 1987 amendment to the Air Act?
x: The 1987 amendment expanded the definition of air pollutant to include noise.

s: Who is empowered to declare an area as an air pollution control area under the Air Act, 1981?
x: The State Government may declare an air pollution control area under Chapter IV, particularly Sections 19 to 31, of the Air Act.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Air Act, 1981 – Declaration of air pollution control areas
Water Cess Act, 1977 – Cess on water consumed by specified industries
Air Act amendment, 1987 – Inclusion of noise in the definition of air pollutant
Water Act, 1974 – Inclusion of noise in the definition of air pollutant
x: Noise was added by the 1987 Air Act amendment; the Water Act, 1974 deals with standards for discharge of effluents.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Water Act, 1974 and the Air Act, 1981?
o: The Water Act aims to maintain and restore the wholesomeness of water
The Air Act has 7 chapters and 54 sections
The Water Act has 8 chapters and 64 sections
Declaring pollution control areas is a special feature of the Water Act
x: Declaring air pollution control areas is the Air Act's special power, not the Water Act's.

s: Which of the following statements about the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 is incorrect?
o: It provides for the prevention, control and abatement of air pollution.
x: Option C is incorrect: the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981, was amended in 1987, not 1991.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Boards under the Air Act, 1981?
o: The CPCB was originally set up under the Water Act
The Air Act created an entirely separate set of Boards unrelated to the Water Act
The existing CPCB was assigned air-pollution functions
The SPCBs enforce the Air Act in the States
x: The Air Act used the same Boards: the CPCB, set up under the Water Act, got air functions and SPCBs enforce it in States.

s: On which date did the Air Act, 1981 come into force?
x: The Air Act was enacted on 29 March 1981 and came into force on 16 May 1981.

s: How many chapters and sections does the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 have?
x: The Air Act has 7 chapters and 54 sections, against the Water Act's 8 chapters and 64 sections.

s: Which Article of the Constitution contains the Fundamental Duty to protect and improve the natural environment and to have compassion for living creatures?
x: Article 51A(g) asks citizens to protect and improve the natural environment and to have compassion for living creatures.

s:
Assertion (A): Article 48A directs the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.
Reason (R): Article 48A was introduced through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: Article 48A directs the State to protect the environment, forests and wildlife, and the 42nd Amendment (1976) added it. When it was added does not explain what it says, so R does not explain A.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment Act inserted Articles 48A and 51A(g) into the Constitution?
x: Both Articles were inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

s: Into which Article have courts read the right to a clean and healthy environment?
x: Article 21 (right to life) has been read to include a clean and healthy environment.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about constitutional provisions on the environment?
o: Article 48A is a Directive Principle addressed to the State
Article 51A(g) is a Fundamental Duty of citizens
Article 253 is the basis of the EP Act, 1986
Article 48A is a Fundamental Duty of citizens
x: Article 48A is a DPSP placing the duty on the State; the citizen's duty is in Article 51A(g).

s: Who grants Consent to Establish (CTE) and Consent to Operate (CTO) to polluting industries?
x: Both consents are given by the State Pollution Control Board: CTE before setting up the unit and CTO before production begins.

s: Which new category of industries has been introduced for essential environmental services such as Compressed Biogas?
x: The Blue category was introduced for essential environmental services, with Compressed Biogas cited as an example.

s: Which of the following pairs (CPCB category – pollution score) is correctly matched?
x: Red corresponds to a score of 60 and above, Orange to 41–59, Green to 21–40 and White to 20 or less.

s: On what is the CPCB's colour categorisation of industries based?
o: Energy consumption, exports and tax contribution
Land area, workforce and annual turnover
Water availability, raw material cost and product demand
Emissions, effluents and hazardous waste generated
x: The basis of the colour categories is the pollution potential represented by emissions, effluents and hazardous waste generated.

s: Under the consent reform introduced in January 2026, which of the following is correct?
o: A single application covers Air and Water consents as well as waste authorisations, and CTO remains valid until cancelled.
A single application is available only for mining projects.
Only waste authorisations are covered and CTO is abolished.
Separate applications remain compulsory and CTO expires annually.
x: The January 2026 reform provides for a single application for Air and Water consents plus waste authorisations, while consent to operate remains valid until cancelled.

s: Which CPCB category of industries is practically non-polluting and needs no consent?
x: White (pollution index 20 or less) needs no consent; Blue is for essential environmental services.

s: When must Consent to Establish (CTE) be obtained from the SPCB?
x: CTE is taken before setting up; Consent to Operate (CTO) is taken before production.

s: Under the CPCB colour categorisation, which category covers industries with a Pollution Index of 41 to 59?
x: Red is 60 and above, Orange 41-59, Green 21-40 and White 20 or less.

s: Which Act decriminalised the penalty regime under the Environment (Protection) Act?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977
x: The Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 decriminalised the penalty regime under the Environment (Protection) Act.

s: What was the original maximum punishment provided under the Environment (Protection) Act for an offence?
o: Only a written warning issued by the Central Government
Up to 5 years’ imprisonment or a fine of Rs 1 lakh, with Rs 5,000 per day for a continuing offence
Life imprisonment and forfeiture of all property
Up to 2 years’ imprisonment or a fine of Rs 10,000, with no continuing penalty
x: The original penalty was imprisonment up to five years or a fine up to Rs 1 lakh, with an additional Rs 5,000 per day for a continuing offence.

s: After the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 amended the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991, where are penalty rates specified?
x: The amendment replaced imprisonment with penalties and shifted penalty rates from the Act to the rules.

s: After the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023, to which body do appeals against penalties under the EP Act lie?
x: Penalties are fixed by an adjudicating officer and appeals go to the NGT.

s: After the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023, who fixes monetary penalties under the EP Act?
x: The Act decriminalised the EPA penalty regime; an adjudicating officer fixes penalties.

s: The Jan Vishwas amendment raised relief for death under the PLI Act, 1991 from Rs 25,000 to how much?
x: Relief for death was raised from Rs 25,000 to Rs 5 lakh.

s: Which body was renamed the Central Pollution Control Board by the 1988 amendment to the Water Act?
o: Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution
x: The Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution, created in 1974, was renamed the CPCB by the 1988 amendment.

s: In which year was the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977 subsumed in GST?
x: The water cess, levied on water consumed by specified industries and local authorities, was subsumed with GST in 2017.

s: The Water Act, 1974 was enacted under Article 252 of the Constitution. What is the implication of this arrangement?
o: It applies to States that adopt it through the constitutionally prescribed process.
It can be enforced only after approval by the Supreme Court.
It automatically applies only to Union Territories.
It applies exclusively to subjects in the Union List.
x: Article 252 permits Parliament to legislate on a State subject when States adopt the required resolution; the law applies in the States adopting it.

s: How many chapters and sections does the Water Act, 1974 have?
x: The Water Act has 8 chapters and 64 sections; the Air Act has 7 chapters and 54 sections.

s: To which fund are the proceeds of the Water Cess credited?
x: Water Cess goes to the Consolidated Fund of India; the EP Fund is kept in the Public Account.

s: Which Section of the Water Act, 1974 empowers directions including environmental compensation?
x: Section 33A of the Water Act provides for directions; Section 31A is the Air Act equivalent.

s: What is the main purpose of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974?
o: To prevent and control water pollution and maintain or restore the wholesomeness of water
To levy a cess on water used by industries
To regulate groundwater extraction by farmers
To supply drinking water to rural areas
x: The Water Act aims to prevent and control water pollution and keep water wholesome; the cess is levied under the 1977 Act.

s: What is the jail term for offences under the Water Act, 1974?
x: The Water Act provides 1.5 to 6 years' jail; up to 5 years is the original EPA penalty.

s: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board was established in which year?
x: The APPCB was set up in 1976 under the Water Act.

s: Which of the following best describes the statutory role of the AP Pollution Control Board?
o: It implements the Water, Air and Environment Protection Acts and specified waste-management rules in Andhra Pradesh.
It administers only the Wildlife Protection Act in Andhra Pradesh.
It functions exclusively as an appellate judicial tribunal for environmental disputes.
It regulates only municipal drinking-water supply and not industrial pollution.
x: The APPCB implements the Water Act, Air Act and Environment (Protection) Act, along with rules relating to hazardous, biomedical, plastic and solid waste.

s: Which of the following is an additional regulatory activity of the AP Pollution Control Board?
o: Granting forest clearance for diversion of forest land
x: The APPCB issues siting guidelines for industries and also prepares SOPs for marine outfall monitoring and hazardous waste.

s: The power of Pollution Control Boards to levy environmental compensation under Section 31A of the Air Act and Section 33A of the Water Act was upheld subject to which limitation?
o: It may be exercised without any connection to actual or imminent harm.
It may be exercised only against government-owned industries.
It may be exercised only when environmental harm is clear or imminent.
It may be exercised only after a criminal conviction.
x: The power to levy compensation has been upheld, but its exercise must be connected with clear or imminent environmental harm.

s: Under the computerised inspection-allocation system used for ease of doing business, which industries are inspected more frequently?
o: All industries at exactly the same frequency
x: The system allocates inspections based on risk, with high-risk industries inspected more often.

s: What is the name of the online consent system of the AP Pollution Control Board?
x: APPCB uses OCMMS (Online Consent Management and Monitoring System) for faster, transparent consents.

s: Besides its head office at Vijayawada, how many offices does the AP Pollution Control Board have?
x: APPCB has its head office at Vijayawada with 3 Zonal and 13 Regional offices.

s:
Consider the following statements about the AP Pollution Control Board:
1. Its head office is at Vijayawada.
2. It was set up in 1976 under the Air Act, 1981.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: APPCB's head office is at Vijayawada; it was set up in 1976 under the Water Act, 1974, as the Air Act came only in 1981.

s: In M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India, in which of the following did the Supreme Court hold environmental protection to be included?
x: The Court held that environmental protection is inherently included within Corporate Social Responsibility.

s: In Vanashakti v. Union of India, how was ex post facto environmental clearance held to be possible?
o: Payment of a penalty, in every case
An administrative order overriding the EIA Notification, 2006
x: Ex post facto clearance is not available merely on payment of a penalty; Article 142 may be applied only in fit cases.

s: The principle of absolute liability was laid down in which case?
o: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum gas leak)
x: Absolute liability came from the Oleum gas leak case (Shriram plant, Delhi, 1985).

s: In which case did the Supreme Court first apply the polluter pays principle?
o: M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India
x: The Bichhri (Udaipur) H-acid sludge case, ICELA 1996, was the first SC application of polluter pays.

s: The precautionary principle was upheld in which case concerning tanneries?
x: Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum (1996) concerned tanneries and held both principles part of the law of the land.

s: In M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath, the public trust doctrine was applied to a motel on which river?
x: The case concerned a motel on the Beas; the lease was quashed under the public trust doctrine.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Oleum gas leak case:
1. It laid down the principle of absolute liability.
2. It concerned the Shriram plant in Delhi.
3. It applied the public trust doctrine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Oleum case (1985) laid down absolute liability for the Shriram plant leak; public trust was applied in M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath.

s: Where did the H-acid sludge pollution dealt with in the Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action case (1996) take place?
x: The ICELA (1996) case on H-acid sludge at Bichhri near Udaipur was the first Supreme Court use of the polluter pays principle.

s: The Bichhri village of the polluter pays case (Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action, 1996) is in which State?
x: Bichhri is near Udaipur in Rajasthan, where chemical units dumped H-acid sludge.

s: The Oleum gas leak case (1985), which laid down the principle of absolute liability, was heard by a Bench led by which Chief Justice?
x: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum gas leak, Shriram plant, Delhi) was decided by a Bench led by CJ P.N. Bhagwati.

s: In which year did the National Green Tribunal Act come into force on 18 October?
x: The NGT Act 2010 came into force on 18 October 2010.

s: Which of the following is NOT a place of sitting of the National Green Tribunal?
x: NGT sits at New Delhi (principal), Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai; Mumbai is not a seat.

s: Where is the principal seat of the National Green Tribunal?
x: The principal seat is New Delhi; Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai are other sittings.

s: Within how many days does an appeal against an NGT order lie to the Supreme Court?
x: Appeals go to the Supreme Court within 90 days.

s: Within what time does the NGT aim to dispose of cases?
x: The NGT aims to dispose of cases within 6 months.

s: For what purpose was the National Green Tribunal set up?
o: Effective and speedy disposal of cases on environmental protection and conservation of forests
x: The NGT was set up to decide environmental and forest cases quickly; standards and consents are the work of pollution control boards.

s: What is the nature of the National Green Tribunal?
o: Statutory body with powers similar to a civil court
Executive body with only advisory jurisdiction
Constitutional body with only administrative powers
x: The NGT is a statutory, not constitutional, body with civil-court powers in matters within its jurisdiction.

s: The establishment of the National Green Tribunal gives effect, in the environmental context, to which Fundamental Right?
o: Right to constitutional remedies under Article 32
x: The NGT gives effect to the right to a healthy environment, which is treated as part of the right to life under Article 21.

s: Within how many days does an appeal against an order of the National Green Tribunal lie to the Supreme Court?
x: An appeal against an NGT order may be filed before the Supreme Court within 90 days.

s: When was the National Green Tribunal set up?
x: The NGT Act was passed on 2 June 2010, the Tribunal was set up on 18 October 2010 and it started functioning in July 2011.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the National Green Tribunal is incorrect?
o: The NGT was established on October 18, 2010.
The constitutional anchor of the NGT is Article 28.
Justice Lokeshwar Singh Panta was the first Chairperson of the NGT.
The NGT was established under the NGT Act, 2010.
x: Option B is incorrect: the NGT's constitutional basis is Article 21 (the right to life, read to include a healthy environment), not Article 28. Justice Lokeshwar Singh Panta was its first chair.

s: Which of the following is a zonal bench location of the National Green Tribunal?
x: Pune is a zonal bench; New Delhi hosts the Principal Bench and Jodhpur and Shillong are circuit benches.

s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal?
x: Justice Lokeshwar Singh Panta was the first NGT Chairperson; Justice Prakash Shrivastava is the current one.

s: Besides the Chairperson, how many Judicial and Expert Members does the National Green Tribunal have?
x: The NGT has a Chairperson with 10 to 20 Judicial and 10 to 20 Expert Members.

s: Which of the following is a circuit bench, not a zonal bench, of the National Green Tribunal?
x: Jodhpur, Shimla and Shillong are circuit benches; Pune, Kolkata, Bhopal and Chennai are zonal benches.

s: When did the National Green Tribunal start functioning?
x: The NGT Act was passed on 2 June 2010, the Tribunal was set up on 18 October 2010 and it started functioning in July 2011.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Green Tribunal:
1. Its zonal bench in western India is at Mumbai.
2. It aims to dispose of cases within 6 months.
3. It is a statutory, not a constitutional, body.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct; the zonal bench is at Pune, not Mumbai.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Green Tribunal?
o: It was set up under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
It is bound by all the procedures of the Code of Civil Procedure
It follows the principles of natural justice
Its principal bench is at New Delhi
x: The NGT is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure; it is guided by the principles of natural justice.

s: After which two countries did India become the third country to set up a specialised environmental tribunal?
x: With the NGT in 2010, India became the third country with a specialised environmental tribunal, after Australia and New Zealand.

s: On which date was the National Green Tribunal Act passed?
x: The NGT Act was passed on 2 June 2010; the Tribunal was set up on 18 October 2010 and began work in July 2011.

s: Who is qualified to be appointed Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal?
o: A judge of the Supreme Court or a Chief Justice of a High Court
An environmental scientist with 15 years' experience
x: The Chairperson is a judge of the Supreme Court or Chief Justice of a High Court; in practice a retired SC judge.

s: Who is the Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal as of 2026?
x: Justice Prakash Shrivastava heads the NGT; Justice Lokeshwar Singh Panta was its first Chairperson.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: River-valley projects — first sector appraised in India
LG Polymers gas leak — Visakhapatnam, 2020 — National Green Tribunal
Great Nicobar EIA — absence of any baseline data collection
NEPA — first EIA law — United States, 1969
x: The Great Nicobar EIA was criticised for thin baseline data, not for the complete absence of baseline data collection. The other pairs are correctly matched.

s: Within what time did the NGT's August 2023 direction ask the Border Roads Organisation to plant the trees?
x: The NGT directed the plantation of the trees within one month.

s: After the May 2020 styrene leak at LG Polymers, Visakhapatnam, what interim deposit did the NGT order?
x: The NGT ordered LG Polymers to make an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Great Nicobar project—High-Powered Committee on NGT directions
Sewage in drinking water—suo motu notice to Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
Styrene leak—Maharashtra and West Bengal waste-management fines
x: The styrene leak concerned LG Polymers at Visakhapatnam and led to an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore. Maharashtra and West Bengal were associated with fines for waste mismanagement.

s:
Consider the following statements about the NGT and the CPCB:
1. The NGT is a judicial tribunal.
2. The CPCB is a statutory regulator under the Water Act, 1974.
3. The CPCB can issue binding directions to the NGT.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; it is the NGT that can direct the CPCB, not the reverse.

s: In which year was the National Environment Appellate Authority Act enacted?
x: The NEAA Act was enacted in 1997; the National Environment Tribunal Act in 1995.

s: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 and the NEAA Act, 1997 were repealed by which Section of the NGT Act?
x: Section 38 of the NGT Act repealed both; pending NEAA cases moved to the NGT.

s: With which of the following did the National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 deal?
x: The NET Act 1995 covered hazardous-substance accidents; the NEAA Act 1997 covered appeals against clearances.

s: In 2014, the NGT banned which practice in Meghalaya?
x: The NGT banned rat-hole mining in Meghalaya in 2014.

s: In 2022, the NGT fined which States for waste mismanagement?
x: The NGT fined Maharashtra and West Bengal in 2022 for waste mismanagement.

s: The National Green Tribunal directed southern States and Puducherry to execute action plans under which programme?
x: The NGT directed southern States and Puducherry to execute action plans under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP).

s: Which body adjudicates environmental disputes and awards compensation?
x: The NGT is adjudicatory and awards compensation; the CPCB regulates, sets standards and monitors pollution.

s: Which of the following Acts is outside the jurisdiction of the National Green Tribunal?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
x: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Forest Rights Act are outside the NGT's listed scope; the BD Act and EP Act are covered.

s: Why was the National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 distinctive?
o: Strict liability for accidents involving hazardous substances
Establishment of the Central Pollution Control Board
x: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 provided for strict liability in cases of accidents involving hazardous substances.

s: The NGT combines which two roles associated earlier with separate environmental institutions?
o: Original jurisdiction over environmental disputes and the appellate role of the NEAA
x: The NGT combines original jurisdiction over environmental disputes with the appellate role earlier performed by the NEAA.

s: Which body took over the role of the National Environment Appellate Authority set up under its 1997 Act?
x: The NEAA no longer exists in its original form; its role passed to the NGT.

s: Which Act repealed the National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995, which never came into force?
x: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 was never brought into force and was repealed by the NGT Act, 2010.

s: How many Acts are listed in Schedule I of the NGT Act, under the Tribunal's jurisdiction?
x: Seven Acts, from the Water Act 1974 to the Biological Diversity Act 2002, are in Schedule I.

s: Which of the following Acts is within the jurisdiction of the National Green Tribunal?
x: The Public Liability Insurance Act 1991 is in Schedule I; the Wildlife Act 1972 and the Forest Rights Act 2006 are outside the NGT.

s: What was the National Environment Appellate Authority Act, 1997 meant to hear?
x: The NEAA heard appeals against environmental clearances; strict liability for hazardous accidents was the NET Act 1995.

s: In January 2022, the National Green Tribunal constituted a mission on which of the following?
o: Management and utilisation of fly ash
x: In January 2022 the NGT set up the Fly Ash Management and Utilization Mission.

s: In which year was the National Environment Appellate Authority Act passed?
x: The NEAA Act, 1997 dealt with appeals against environmental clearances; the National Environment Tribunal Act came in 1995.

s: The global origin of Environmental Impact Assessment is linked to the National Environmental Policy Act of which country and year?
x: The global origin of EIA is associated with the United States National Environmental Policy Act, enacted in 1969.

s: When did the Planning Commission ask the Department of Science and Technology to examine river-valley projects?
x: India's EIA process began in 1976-77 when the Planning Commission asked DST to examine river-valley projects.

s: Under the EIA framework, when must environmental clearance be obtained as a rule?
o: After an environmental audit finds non-compliance
Only for products assessed through LCA
x: Prior environmental clearance is mandatory; post-facto approval, where recognised at all, is only a narrow exception.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Environmental Impact Assessment identifies, predicts and evaluates the environmental impacts of development projects.
R2 Code of Practices is a framework for environmentally responsible electronics recycling.
R2 Code of Practices is another name for Environmental Impact Assessment.
EIA assesses the likely environmental consequences of a proposed project or activity before implementation.
x: Option C is incorrect: R2 is a code for responsible electronics recycling. EIA is the process of assessing a project's likely environmental impact before it starts.

s: In which year was EIA first used in India?
x: EIA was first used in 1978, after the 1976-77 DST review of river-valley projects.

s: To which of the following does the R2 Code of Practices relate?
x: R2 Code of Practices is not EIA; it is for responsible electronics recycling.

s: A government is assessing the environmental implications of a new transport policy before individual road projects are selected. Which tool is most appropriate?
x: Strategic Environmental Assessment examines policies, plans and programmes upstream of individual projects. A project-level EIA is conducted for a specific project, whereas an environmental audit is generally an after-the-fact compliance check.

s: Which of the following pairs (tool – scope) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Environmental audit – A project evaluated before it starts
Life-Cycle Assessment – A product or process across its whole life cycle
Environmental Impact Assessment – A project evaluated before it starts
Cumulative Impact Assessment – Combined effect of several projects in one area
x: An environmental audit is a compliance check of an operating unit after the fact; evaluation before a project starts is EIA.

s: Who formulated the 12 principles of green chemistry?
x: The 12 principles of green chemistry (prevent waste, atom economy, safer solvents, renewable feedstocks, design for degradation) were set out by Anastas and Warner in 1998. The Brundtland Commission (1987) defined sustainable development; Rachel Carson wrote Silent Spring (1962); the Club of Rome issued Limits to Growth (1972).

s: The proposal for sector-wide EIAs is intended primarily to strengthen which approach?
x: Sector-wide EIAs are intended to incorporate strategic and cumulative perspectives, allowing impacts across a sector or region to be assessed rather than examining projects in isolation.

s: Which of the following describes cleaner production?
o: Treats pollution only after it has been generated at the end of a pipe
Cuts waste and pollution at the source through process change or input substitution
Replaces environmental assessment with an operating-unit audit
Focuses exclusively on disposal of hazardous waste
x: Cleaner production is preventive: it reduces waste and pollution at source through measures such as process change and input substitution, rather than relying mainly on end-of-pipe treatment.

s: On which of the following does Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA) focus?
o: A specific project before it starts
A product or process from cradle to grave
x: LCA covers a product's life cycle; EIA covers a project, SEA policies and an audit a running unit.

s: Which tool checks the compliance of a running unit after the fact?
x: An environmental audit assesses compliance of a running unit after the fact.

s: Which tool assesses the combined effect of several projects in one area?
x: Cumulative Impact Assessment examines the combined effect of several projects in one area.

s: According to the final Vanashakti verdict of 29 July 2026, which test must any ex post facto environmental clearance satisfy?
o: Article 252 read with the Water Act, 1974
Article 323B read with the NGT Act, 2010
x: The Court held that ex post facto EC must meet Articles 14 and 21 (a proportionality test), while the Supreme Court keeps its power under Article 142. Articles 48A and 51A(g) are a Directive Principle and a Fundamental Duty, not the test laid down. Article 252 is the Water Act's basis; Article 323B concerns tribunals generally.

s: Which case examined the 2020 exemption for extraction of ordinary earth for linear projects?
x: Noble M. Paikada examined the 2020 ordinary-earth exemption; Common Cause concerned Odisha mining beyond environmental clearance.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Alembic Pharmaceuticals v. Rohit Prajapati?
o: The 2002 MoEF circular permitting such clearance was quashed
The Court directed closure of every project concerned
Ex post facto clearance was held contrary to the EIA regime
x: The Court imposed compensation instead of ordering closure of every project.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Vanashakti litigation?
o: The May 2025 ruling struck down the 2017 Notification and the 2021 Office Memorandum
The May 2025 ruling was recalled unanimously in November 2025
About Rs 20,000 crore worth of projects was reported to be at stake
The recall relied on D. Swamy (2021) and Pahwa Plastics (2022), among others
x: The recall in November 2025 was by a 2:1 majority, not unanimous.

s: The final Vanashakti verdict of 29 July 2026 prospectively nullified which instrument?
x: The verdict prospectively nullified the 2021 Office Memorandum, while earlier clearances under the 2017 Notification and the 2021 OM survived.

s: Which Chief Justice of India headed the bench that delivered the final Vanashakti verdict of 29 July 2026?
x: The CJI Surya Kant bench prospectively nullified the 2021 OM.

s: In Common Cause (2017), what did the Supreme Court order mining firms in Odisha that mined beyond their environmental clearance to pay?
o: 50% of the value of the illegally mined mineral
10% of the value as a token penalty
100% of the value of the illegally mined mineral
Only the cost of tree planting
x: In Common Cause (2017) the Court ordered payment of 100% of the value of mineral mined beyond the EC.

s: Submergence in which States is the main issue in the inter-state dispute over the Polavaram project?
x: The Polavaram inter-state dispute concerns submergence in neighbouring Odisha and Chhattisgarh and was raised before the Supreme Court.

s: In November 2017, under which category did the NGT hold the Amaravati capital project to fall?
x: The NGT refused to set aside the 2015 EC, held Amaravati Category B and added supervisory and implementation committees.

s: Which State sought a review of the Polavaram project's EIA in the Supreme Court?
x: Telangana sought an EIA review of Polavaram (APPSC 2018); submergence affects Odisha and Chhattisgarh.

s: In December 2021, about how much environmental compensation did the NGT order the Andhra Pradesh government to pay for violations in the Polavaram, Pattiseema, Purushottapatnam and Chintalapudi projects?
x: On 2 December 2021 the NGT ordered about Rs 243 crore in all; Polavaram's share was about Rs 120 crore.

s: To which body did the NGT (2021) direct the Andhra Pradesh government to pay environmental compensation for the Polavaram and lift irrigation projects?
x: On 2 December 2021 the NGT ordered the AP government to pay about Rs 243 crore environmental compensation to the APPCB for violations in the Polavaram, Pattiseema, Purushottapatnam and Chintalapudi projects.

s: Through which amendment was a public hearing made mandatory under the 1994 EIA framework?
x: Mandatory public hearing was added by the 1997 amendment to the 1994 framework.

s: The EIA Notification, 2006 made environmental clearance compulsory for how many project categories?
x: The 2006 notification made environmental clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.

s: In which year was India's first EIA Notification under the Environment (Protection) Act issued on 27 January?
x: The EIA Notification, 1994 was issued on 27 January 1994; earlier clearance was only administrative, and the 2006 notification replaced it.

s: On which date was the EIA Notification, 2006 issued?
x: The EIA Notification of 14 September 2006 replaced the first notification of 27 January 1994.

s: Which EIA stage identifies key issues and sets the Terms of Reference?
x: Scoping fixes key issues and Terms of Reference; screening decides whether EIA is needed and appraisal evaluates the final report.

s: Which is the first stage of the EIA process?
x: The EIA sequence is screening, scoping, appraisal and decision.

s: Which of the following pairs (EIA stage – what happens) is correctly matched?
o: Monitoring – Clearance granted with conditions or rejected
Decision – Implementation of the EMP is checked
Appraisal – Expert committee evaluates the EIA report
Appraisal – Clearance granted with conditions or rejected
x: At appraisal the expert committee evaluates the EIA report; at decision clearance is granted or rejected, and monitoring checks EMP implementation.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about EIA project categories?
o: Category B projects are appraised by the central Expert Appraisal Committee
Category B projects are cleared by SEIAA
Category A projects are appraised by the central EAC
Category A projects are cleared by MoEFCC
x: Category B projects are appraised by the State Expert Appraisal Committee and cleared by SEIAA; the central EAC appraises Category A.

s: At which stage of the EIA process are alternatives compared?
x: Impact prediction includes comparison of alternatives; baseline data surveys the existing environment and mitigation planning includes the EMP.

s: Implementation of the Environment Management Plan is checked at which EIA stage?
x: Monitoring, the last stage, checks implementation of the EMP.

s: The EIA Notification, 2006 introduced which major change in the basis for appraisal?
o: A shift from investment size to impact potential
A shift from public consultation to administrative approval only
A shift from project categories to product certification
A shift from impact potential to investment size
x: The 2006 notification shifted the test from investment size to impact potential and made clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.

s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, which of the following is true of Category B2 projects?
o: Require a full EIA by MoEFCC
Are appraised by the central EAC
x: Category B1 projects require an EIA while B2 projects do not; both fall under state-level appraisal and clearance.

s: What is the status of the Draft EIA Notification, 2020?
o: Praised for longer public consultation periods than 2006
Notable for abolishing penalties for violations
Not finalised, and criticised for proposing post-facto clearance
x: The 2020 draft was not finalised and was contested, particularly for post-facto clearance and shorter consultation periods.

s: Under the Draft EIA Notification, 2020, who alone could report violations?
x: The draft restricted reporting of violations to the violator or the government, one of its contested provisions.

s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, who clears Category A projects?
x: Category A projects are appraised by the central EAC and cleared by MoEFCC.

s: Under the EIA Notification, 1994, in which Schedule were projects needing MoEF clearance listed?
x: Under the 1994 notification, Schedule I projects needed MoEF clearance.

s: Under the Draft EIA Notification, 2020, the notice period for a public hearing was proposed to be cut from 30 days to how many days?
x: The draft 2020 notification proposed cutting the public hearing notice from 30 to 20 days, one of its contested points.

s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, which category of projects is appraised by the SEAC and needs an EIA report?
x: B1 projects are appraised by SEAC and need an EIA; B2 projects need no EIA; Category A goes to the central EAC.

s: Who presides over the public hearing conducted by the State Pollution Control Board?
x: The State Pollution Control Board conducts the hearing, while the District Collector presides over it.

s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, within how many days must a public hearing be completed?
x: The hearing notice must be given at least 30 days in advance and the hearing completed within 45 days.

s: In the EIA process, who decides whether a project is 'strategic' and thus exempt from public hearing?
x: The Central Government decides 'strategic' status (criticised as arbitrary); the SPCB only conducts the public hearing.

s: Which of the following is NOT exempt from an EIA public hearing?
x: Defence, strategic, B2 and industrial-estate units are exempt; Category A projects are not.

s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, what is the minimum notice for a public hearing?
x: Notice must be at least 30 days; the 2020 draft proposed cutting it to 20 days.

s: An APPCB public hearing in May 2026, where the draft EIA was called error-ridden, was on a Water Aerodrome at which site?
x: The hearing concerned a Water Aerodrome at Prakasam Barrage, Vijayawada.

s: What is PARIVESH?
o: A single-window portal for online environment, forest, wildlife and CRZ clearances
A programme for preparing baseline biodiversity data
A committee for appraisal of Category A projects
x: PARIVESH is an online single-window platform for environment, forest, wildlife and Coastal Regulation Zone clearances.

s: Which of the following was a provision of the July 2026 amendment to the EIA framework?
o: The Centre may remove EAC, SEAC or SEIAA members mid-term for persistent delays.
Scientists alone must replace all administrative members.
All Category B projects must automatically be transferred to the central EAC.
State committees may retain proposals indefinitely without escalation.
x: The amendment permits the Centre to remove members of EAC, SEAC or SEIAA mid-term for persistent delays. It also introduced an escalation mechanism rather than automatic transfer of all Category B projects to the central EAC.

s: Under the 2026 backup arrangement for environmental appraisal bodies, which body stands in for SEIAA?
x: SAEIA is the backup for SEIAA, while SCEIA is the backup for SEAC.

s: In which year was the PARIVESH single-window clearance portal launched?
x: PARIVESH (2018) handles environment, forest, wildlife and CRZ clearances online.

s: What is the upper age limit for members of the appraisal committees (EAC/SEAC)?
x: Members serve 3-4 years, at most two terms, with an age limit of 70.

s: Under the July 2026 amendment, to which body may a proposal escalate if a State Expert Appraisal Committee fails to decide it within 120 days?
o: The new Standing Committee on Environmental Impact Assessment on PARIVESH
x: The July 2026 amendment provides for escalation after 120 days to the new SCEIA through PARIVESH.

s: Which one of the following has been suggested as a measure to address the criticism that EIA consultants may lack independence?
o: Transfer of EIA preparation entirely to project proponents
Permitting post-facto clearances as a routine measure
Creation of an independent EIA authority
x: An independent EIA authority has been suggested to improve the credibility and independence of environmental assessments.

s: A major criticism of EIA reports in India is that they are often prepared by whom?
o: Consultants paid by the project proponents
x: EIA reports are often prepared by proponent-paid consultants; another criticism is the lack of a central baseline data bank.

s: In which year was the Ministry of Environment and Forests renamed MoEFCC?
x: The sequence is Department of Environment 1980, Air Act 1981, MoEF 1985 and renaming to MoEFCC in 2014.

s: In which year was the Department of Environment created in India?
x: The Department of Environment was created in 1980; it became the Ministry of Environment and Forests in 1985.

s: In which year was the Ministry of Environment and Forests (MoEF) formed?
x: MoEF was formed in 1985, after the Department of Environment (1980); it was renamed MoEFCC in 2014.

s: Which one of the following bodies replaced the Environment Pollution (Prevention and Control) Authority (EPCA) in the National Capital Region and adjoining areas?
x: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), established under the CAQM Act, 2021, replaced EPCA in the NCR and adjoining areas.

s: The National Mission for Clean Ganga is the successor set-up to which body?
x: NMCG is the successor set-up to the National Ganga River Basin Authority (NGRBA), which was established in 2009 under the Environment (Protection) Act.

s: Under which provision was the Central Ground Water Authority constituted in 1997?
x: The CGWA was set up in 1997 under Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

s: In which year was the Act setting up the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and adjoining areas passed?
x: The CAQM was set up under the CAQM Act 2021 and replaced the EPCA.

s: The National River Conservation Plan covers pollution abatement in how many rivers?
x: NRCP covers 38 rivers in 16 States, outside the Ganga basin.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Forest Survey of India?
x: The Forest Survey of India, like the Wildlife Institute of India, is at Dehradun; BSI is at Kolkata and GBPNIHE at Kosi-Katarmal, Almora.

s: Where is the Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History (SACON) located?
x: SACON is at Coimbatore; IITR is at Lucknow, CMLRE at Kochi and ZSI at Kolkata.

s: Where is the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI) located?
x: NEERI is at Nagpur. Lucknow hosts IITR (toxicology); Dehradun hosts WII and FSI; Coimbatore hosts SACON.

s: Where is the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) located?
x: WII and the Forest Survey of India are both at Dehradun.

s: Where are the Botanical Survey of India and the Zoological Survey of India both headquartered?
x: BSI and ZSI are both at Kolkata.

s: Which pair of institute and location is correctly matched?
x: GBPNIHE is at Kosi-Katarmal, Almora; IITR is at Lucknow, SACON at Coimbatore and NEERI at Nagpur.

s: Where is the Indian Institute of Toxicology Research (IITR) located?
x: IITR is at Lucknow; NEERI is at Nagpur and WII at Dehradun.

s: Where is the Centre for Marine Living Resources and Ecology (CMLRE), which hosts the 'Bhavasagara' deep-sea fauna repository, located?
x: CMLRE, home of the Bhavasagara deep-sea fauna repository, is at Kochi.

s: In 2022, ENVIS, the network of environmental information centres, was renamed as which of the following?
x: ENVIS (1982) was renamed EIACP in 2022 and aligned with Mission LiFE.

s: In which year was the Forest Survey of India established?
x: The Forest Survey of India, at Dehradun, was set up in 1981.

s: In which year was ENVIS, the network of environmental information centres, set up?
x: ENVIS was set up in 1982 and renamed EIACP in 2022.

s: Under whose authority, and under which Act, was the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board established in 1976?
o: Government of India under the Air Act, 1981
Government of Andhra Pradesh under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
National Green Tribunal under the Water Act, 1974
Government of Andhra Pradesh under the Water Act, 1974
x: The APPCB was established in 1976 by the Government of Andhra Pradesh under the Water Act, 1974.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board?
o: Its enforcement role is limited to the Water Act alone
It enforces rules on hazardous, biomedical, plastic and solid waste
It issues siting guidelines and SOPs for marine outfalls and hazardous waste
x: APPCB enforces the Water Act, the Air Act and the Environment Protection Act, not the Water Act alone.

s: Under the Water and Air Acts, before which step is a 'Consent to Operate' from the State Pollution Control Board needed?
x: Consent to Operate is needed before production or discharge; Consent to Establish is needed before setting up the unit.

s: Who nominates the chairperson of a State Pollution Control Board?
o: Governor on the advice of the NGT
x: An SPCB chair is nominated by the State Government; the CPCB chairman is nominated by the Central Government.

s: Where is the head office of the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board?
x: APPCB has its head office at Vijayawada, with 3 Zonal and 13 Regional offices.

s: Apart from its head office, the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board has how many Regional offices?
x: APPCB has its head office at Vijayawada with 3 Zonal and 13 Regional offices.

s: Which instrument is used in pollution control laboratories to measure heavy metals such as lead and cadmium in samples?
x: An Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometer measures metals in water and soil samples; the others measure wind, pressure and light.

s: On the flood plains of how many polluted rivers is the AP State Biodiversity Board developing biodiversity parks?
x: The AP State Biodiversity Board is creating biodiversity parks on the flood plains of 5 polluted rivers.

s: The Andhra Pradesh State Environment Impact Assessment Authority (AP SEIAA) clears which category of projects under the EIA Notification 2006?
x: AP SEIAA, constituted by MoEF order under Section 3 of the EPA, clears Category B projects.

s: For the disposal of which waste was the Andhra Pradesh Environment Management Corporation (APEMCL) mainly set up?
x: APEMCL handles collection, transport, storage and disposal of industrial waste with APPCB, and is to expand to biomedical, battery and e-waste.

s: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 follows which international agreement?
x: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 gives effect to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).

s: Under India's three-tier biodiversity governance structure, which is the local-level body?
x: The NBA works at the national level, SBBs at the State level and BMCs at the local level.

s: With reference to biopiracy, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Foreigners may access Indian bio-resources without approval if no patent is sought.
Foreigners require approval of the NBA to access bio-resources or traditional knowledge, and NBA approval precedes intellectual property rights on them.
Only local bodies can grant approval for foreign access to traditional knowledge.
NBA approval is required only after intellectual property rights have been granted.
x: Foreigners require NBA approval to access bio-resources or associated traditional knowledge, and such approval precedes the grant of intellectual property rights. Access and benefit-sharing with local communities is also an important safeguard.

s: Where is the headquarters of the National Biodiversity Authority?
x: The National Biodiversity Authority, set up in 2003, has its headquarters in Chennai, not Bengaluru.

s: In which year was the National Biodiversity Authority established?
x: The NBA was set up in 2003 under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.

s: In which year was the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 amended?
x: The Act was amended in 2023 and the Biological Diversity Rules followed in 2024.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: CGWA — Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act
x: NBA is associated with biodiversity governance, not the National Clean Air Programme. CAQM, CGWA and NMCG are correctly matched with their respective legal basis or programme.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Central Pollution Control Board?
o: Its air-pollution functions were added by the EP Act, 1986
It was renamed CPCB by a 1988 amendment
It was constituted in 1974 under the Water Act
It is a statutory body under MoEFCC
x: CPCB's air functions were added by the Air Act, 1981; the EP Act, 1986 only widened its scope.

s: Which body is primarily responsible for enforcing environmental standards under the Environment (Protection) Act framework?
x: The CPCB is the body responsible for enforcing environmental standards under the Environment (Protection) Act framework.

s: Which is the oldest national pollution-control body in India, set up in 1974?
x: The CPCB, set up in 1974, is the oldest national pollution body; the NGT (2010) replaced the NEAA.

s: What is PRANA, a CPCB portal, used to track?
o: Real-time water quality of the Ganga and Yamuna
x: PRANA tracks NCAP; daily AQI bulletins come from the National AQI (2015) and RTWQMS covers real-time Ganga and Yamuna water quality.

s: Under which Act was the Central Pollution Control Board first constituted in 1974?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
x: CPCB was set up in 1974 under the Water Act as the Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution.

s: Who nominates the chairman of the Central Pollution Control Board?
x: CPCB is a statutory body under MoEFCC whose chairman is nominated by the Central Government.

s: In which year was the Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution renamed the Central Pollution Control Board?
x: The 1988 amendment renamed it the Central Pollution Control Board.

s: What is the full form of NAMP, run by the Central Pollution Control Board?
x: NAMP is the National Air Monitoring Programme of the CPCB, with real-time CAAQMS stations.

s: In which year was India's National Air Quality Index (AQI) launched?
x: The National AQI was launched in 2015 and gives daily AQI bulletins.

s: From which Act did the Central Pollution Control Board get its air-pollution functions?
x: Air functions were added by the Air Act, 1981; the EPA 1986 only widened its scope.

s: As of March 2026, how many stations does the National Air Monitoring Programme (NAMP) have?
x: CPCB's NAMP had 1,646 stations in 603 cities in March 2026.

s: What does the CPCB's Real Time Water Quality Monitoring System (RTWQMS) track?
o: Water quality of the Ganga and Yamuna
x: RTWQMS gives real-time water quality of the Ganga and Yamuna.

s: In which year was the Wildlife (Protection) Act enacted?
x: The Wildlife Act dates from 1972, the Water Act 1974, the Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 and the Air Act 1981.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Biological Diversity Act dates from 2002; the EPA is of 1986, the Forest Rights Act 2006 and the NGT Act 2010.

s: Which legislation is associated with biodiversity and benefit sharing?
x: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002, covers biodiversity and access and benefit sharing, following the CBD.

s: Which Act is described as umbrella legislation for environmental protection in India?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
x: The EP Act, 1986 is umbrella legislation; the NGT Act, 2010 relates to environmental justice.

s: In which year was the Forest (Conservation) Act, which regulates forest diversion, enacted?
x: The Forest (Conservation) Act is of 1980; the Wildlife Act is 1972 and the EPA 1986.

s: Where was the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment, 1972, held?
x: The UN Conference on the Human Environment was held in Stockholm, Sweden, from 5 to 16 June 1972.

s: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations Environment Programme, set up in 1972, located?
x: UNEP was established in 1972 and its headquarters is in Nairobi, Kenya.

s: Through which Act were the decisions of the Stockholm Conference implemented in India?
x: The Stockholm decisions were implemented in India through the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: World Environment Day on 5 June was an outcome of the Stockholm Conference, 1972, which also produced UNEP and a 26-principle Declaration.

s: Who was the only visiting head of government at the Stockholm Conference, 1972?
x: Indira Gandhi was the only visiting head of government at Stockholm; she linked poverty and environment.

s: The Stockholm Declaration of 1972 contained how many principles?
x: The Stockholm Declaration had 26 principles; the Rio Declaration of 1992 had 27.

s: In which year was World Environment Day first observed?
x: World Environment Day on 5 June came out of Stockholm 1972 and was first observed in 1973.

s: Which country hosted World Environment Day in 2019?
x: China hosted World Environment Day in 2019; the day is observed on 5 June, a Stockholm 1972 outcome.

s: The 1972 Stockholm Conference was the UN Conference on which of the following?
x: Stockholm 1972 was the UN Conference on the Human Environment; Rio 1992 (UNCED) was on Environment and Development.

s: Who launched the Global 500 awards for protection of the environment in 1987?
x: The Global 500 awards were launched by UNEP in 1987.

s: Where was the Ramsar Convention adopted in 1971?
x: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar in Iran.

s: Where is the Secretariat of the Ramsar Convention located?
x: The Ramsar Convention Secretariat is located at Gland, Switzerland.

s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Rio Earth Summit
2. Ramsar Convention
3. Stockholm Conference
x: The Ramsar Convention dates from 1971, the Stockholm Conference from 1972 and the Rio Earth Summit from 1992.

s: Kolleru Lake is associated with which of the following international conservation designations?
x: Kolleru is a Ramsar wetland of international importance.

s: Which of the following was among the first Indian sites designated under the Ramsar Convention?
x: Chilika Lake, along with Keoladeo National Park, was among the first Indian Ramsar sites, designated on 1 October 1981.

s: Which of the following Indian wetlands are currently on the Montreux Record of the Ramsar Convention?
o: Keoladeo National Park and Loktak Lake
Keoladeo National Park and Wular Lake
x: The Montreux Record lists Ramsar sites under threat; India's sites on it are Keoladeo NP and Loktak Lake. Chilika was on it but was removed after restoration, so options with Chilika are wrong; Kolleru and Wular are not on the Record.

s: Since which year has India been a Party to the Ramsar Convention?
x: India became a Party to the Ramsar Convention in 1982. The Convention itself was signed on 2 February 1971 at Ramsar, Iran.

s: Which were India's first accredited Wetland Cities under the Ramsar Convention (January 2025)?
x: Udaipur and Indore became India's first accredited Wetland Cities in January 2025.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Loktak Lake is in Manipur; Chilika is in Odisha, Keoladeo in Rajasthan and Wular in J&K.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Harike Wetland is located in Punjab.
East Kolkata Wetlands are located in West Bengal.
Sundarban Wetland is located in Odisha.
Kabartal/Kanwar Lake is located in Begusarai, Bihar.
x: Option C is incorrect: the Sundarban wetland is in West Bengal, not Odisha. Harike is in Punjab and Kabartal in Begusarai, Bihar.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three pillars of obligations under the Ramsar Convention?
o: Banning all human use of wetlands
x: Ramsar's pillars are designation, wise use and international cooperation; wise use allows sustainable use.

s: As of 16 October 2026, how many Ramsar sites does India have?
x: On 16 October 2026 India's Ramsar tally reached 103, with the addition of Sukhna Lake (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh).

s: In which year was Kolleru Lake, Andhra Pradesh's only Ramsar site, designated?
x: Kolleru Lake, between the Godavari and Krishna deltas, was designated on 19 August 2002.

s: What was the theme of World Wetlands Day 2017?
x: World Wetlands Day (2 February) in 2017 had the theme 'Wetlands for Disaster Risk Reduction'.

s: Sauj Jheel, which became one of India's Ramsar sites in October 2026, is located in which State?
x: On 16 October 2026 India's Ramsar tally reached 103 with Sukhna Lake (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh).

s: Sukhna Lake, designated a Ramsar site on 16 October 2026, is located in which of the following?
x: Sukhna Lake in Chandigarh and Sauj Jheel in Mainpuri (UP) took India's Ramsar sites to 103.

s: Kolleru Lake, Andhra Pradesh's only Ramsar site, lies between the deltas of which rivers?
x: Kolleru Lake lies between the Godavari and Krishna deltas; it was designated a Ramsar site on 19 August 2002.

s: At Ramsar CoP-15 (July 2025), India's resolution on which theme was adopted?
o: Sustainable lifestyles for wise use of wetlands
x: Ramsar CoP-15 (30 July 2025) adopted India's resolution on sustainable lifestyles for wise use of wetlands.

s: The 'Amrit Dharohar' strategy launched in June 2023 is related to which of the following?
x: Amrit Dharohar (June 2023) is India's strategy for the wise use and conservation of its Ramsar wetlands.

s: Which country hosted the 14th Conference of the Parties (COP-14) of the UNCCD in 2019?
x: India hosted UNCCD COP-14 in 2019; COP-17 is in Mongolia.

s: Which country is the host of COP-17 of the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD)?
x: UNCCD COP-17 is hosted by Mongolia with the theme 'Restoring Land. Restoring Hope'; India hosted COP-14 in 2019.

s: What is the theme of COP-17 of the UNCCD in Mongolia?
x: The UNCCD COP-17 in Mongolia has the theme 'Restoring Land. Restoring Hope'.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The UNCCD was adopted in 1994 and its Secretariat is at Bonn. The World Heritage Secretariat is in Paris, the IWC headquarters is in Cambridge, and the Basel Secretariat is in Geneva.

s: By which year is India to freeze HFCs under the Kigali Amendment?
x: Under the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol, India's HFC freeze year is 2028.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Montreal Protocol — India is a Party
x: The Montreal Protocol was adopted at Montreal in 1987, its Ozone Secretariat is at Nairobi, and India is a Party. Helsinki is not the Secretariat location.

s: On which date is the International Day for Biological Diversity observed?
x: International Day for Biological Diversity is observed annually on 22 May.

s: When did the Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ), the High Seas Treaty, enter into force?
x: The BBNJ Agreement entered into force on 17 January 2026.

s: In which year did India ratify the Basel Convention on hazardous waste?
x: India ratified Basel in June 1992; the Convention was adopted in 1989 and entered into force in 1992.

s: Which one of the following pairs of environmental observance and date is correctly matched?
x: World Wetlands Day is 2 February, the day the Ramsar Convention was adopted. World Wildlife Day is 3 March (CITES signed), so the first two options swap the dates, and 22 May is the International Day for Biological Diversity.

s: What does the BBNJ Agreement mainly deal with?
o: Protection of biodiversity inside national parks
Biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction in the high seas
Biosafety regulation of genetically modified crops
x: The BBNJ Agreement (High Seas Treaty) concerns marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction, i.e. the high seas. It entered into force on 17 January 2026; India signed it in September 2024. Wetlands (Ramsar), national parks and GM-crop biosafety (Cartagena) are covered by other instruments.

s: Where is the secretariat of the World Heritage Convention (1972) located?
x: The World Heritage Convention is a UNESCO convention with its secretariat at Paris; India ratified it in 1977.

s: Which pair of treaty and secretariat is correctly matched?
x: The IWC is at Cambridge, UK; UNCCD is at Bonn, the Ozone Secretariat at Nairobi and the Ramsar Secretariat at Gland.

s: When did India sign the High Seas Treaty (BBNJ Agreement)?
x: India signed the BBNJ Agreement in September 2024; ratification is under way. It entered into force on 17 January 2026.

s: For which period was the UN Decade on Biodiversity declared?
x: The UN Decade on Biodiversity is 2011-2020 (UNGA Res 65/161).

s: On which date is the World Day to Combat Desertification observed?
x: Desertification Day is 17 June; 5 June is World Environment Day, 22 May Biodiversity Day and 16 September Ozone Day.

s: In which year did India ratify the World Heritage Convention (1972)?
x: India ratified UNESCO's World Heritage Convention in 1977; its secretariat is in Paris.

s: In which city was the convention setting up the International Whaling Commission signed in 1946?
x: The whaling convention was signed at Washington in 1946; the IWC secretariat is at Cambridge, UK.

s: Which species is India's single largest earner of access and benefit-sharing income?
x: Red sanders gives about 45% (Rs 120 crore) of India's ABS income.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Kunming-Montreal GBF — adopted in 2000 and entered into force in 2003
Cartagena Protocol — adopted in 2010 and entered into force in 2014
Nagoya Protocol — adopted in 2010 and entered into force in 2014
Aichi Targets — adopted in 2022 for the period 2030–2050
x: The Nagoya Protocol was adopted at COP10, Nagoya, in 2010 and entered into force in 2014. The other pairs are wrong: the Cartagena Protocol was adopted in 2000 and in force in 2003 (not 2010/2014), the KMGBF was adopted in 2022 (not 2000), and the Aichi Targets were adopted in 2010 for 2011-2020 (not 2022 for 2030-2050).

s: In which year did India ratify the Nagoya Protocol?
x: India ratified the Nagoya Protocol in 2012; 2014 is the year the Protocol entered into force.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Nagoya Protocol is a protocol under the Convention on Biological Diversity. The Cartagena Protocol is also under the CBD, while the Nagoya-Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol is linked to the Cartagena Protocol.

s: The Cartagena Protocol mainly regulates the safe transfer, handling and use of which of the following?
o: Carbon credits generated by forest plantations
Endangered species traded across international borders
Living Modified Organisms resulting from modern biotechnology
x: The Cartagena Protocol deals with the safe transfer, handling and use of Living Modified Organisms resulting from modern biotechnology.

s: What does the Nagoya Protocol deal with?
x: Nagoya covers access and benefit sharing; Cartagena covers biosafety, the CBD biodiversity conservation and the UNCCD desertification.

s: The Nagoya-Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol on Liability and Redress (2010) is supplementary to which instrument?
o: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
x: The Nagoya-Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol on Liability and Redress is supplementary to the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety and is therefore connected to the CBD framework.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Cartagena Protocol?
o: Its Biosafety Clearing-House is a laboratory that tests all GM crops before export
Under Advance Informed Agreement, the importing country consents before the first transboundary movement of an LMO
It deals with biosafety and living modified organisms
LMO shipments carry documentation identifying the LMO
x: The Biosafety Clearing-House is an online platform for sharing LMO information and decisions, not a testing laboratory.

s: In India, which body gives approvals for genetically engineered organisms?
x: The Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee approves genetically engineered organisms; MoEF&CC is the nodal ministry for the Cartagena Protocol.

s: Under which convention is the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety (adopted 2000) a protocol?
x: The Cartagena Protocol is under the CBD; it entered into force in 2003 and is named after Cartagena, Colombia.

s: The Nagoya Protocol covers genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge relating to which of the following?
o: Only animal and human genetic material
Plants, animals and microorganisms, but not human genetic material
All genetic material, including human genetic material
x: The Protocol covers plant, animal and microbial genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, while excluding human genetic material.

s: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of the Nagoya Protocol?
o: Compliance against illegal acquisition of genetic resources
Compulsory transfer of all genetic resources to the National Biodiversity Authority
Mutually Agreed Terms for monetary and non-monetary benefits
x: The pillars are prior informed consent, Mutually Agreed Terms for benefit-sharing, and compliance against illegal acquisition. Compulsory transfer of all genetic resources is not a pillar.

s: India submitted its first National Report on the Nagoya Protocol with which of the following figures?
o: 3,556 IRCCs, constituting less than 30% of the global total
1,556 IRCCs, constituting over 60% of the global total
3,556 IRCCs, constituting over 60% of the global total
2,556 IRCCs, constituting over 50% of the global total
x: India's first National Report recorded 3,556 IRCCs, more than 60% of the global total.

s: Under the Cartagena Protocol, which procedure is required before the first transboundary movement of living modified organisms?
x: The Cartagena Protocol uses the advance informed agreement procedure; prior informed consent is a Nagoya pillar.

s: What is the Biosafety Clearing-House under the Cartagena Protocol?
o: A laboratory for testing GM crops
An online platform for information on LMOs
x: The Biosafety Clearing-House is an online platform for LMO information, not a testing lab.

s: Under the Nagoya Protocol, what is research and development on the genetic or biochemical composition of genetic resources called?
x: The Nagoya Protocol defines 'utilisation of genetic resources' as R&D on their genetic and/or biochemical composition.

s: When did the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety enter into force?
x: The Cartagena Protocol was adopted on 29 January 2000 and entered into force on 11 September 2003.

s: Where was the first Meeting of the Parties (COP/MOP-1) to the Cartagena Protocol held in February 2004?
x: COP/MOP-1 of the Cartagena Protocol was held at Kuala Lumpur in February 2004.

s: Through which law does India implement the access and benefit-sharing objectives of the Nagoya Protocol?
x: ABS in India works through the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (amended 2023), with NBA approvals and ABS regulations.

s: In which city was CITES adopted on 3 March 1973?
x: CITES was adopted at Washington, D.C. and entered into force on 1 July 1975; its UNEP-administered Secretariat is in Geneva.

s: Which is the principal Indian law implementing CITES?
x: CITES is implemented in India through the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

s: Which one of the following species is correctly matched with CITES Appendix I?
x: The Indian star tortoise is listed in Appendix I; it was uplisted on India’s proposal at CoP18 in 2019. Red sanders, golden gecko and rosewood are listed in Appendix II.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the CITES Appendices?
o: Appendix III species are listed by one Party seeking others' help to control trade
Appendix II includes species not yet threatened with extinction
Trade in Appendix II species is controlled through permits
Appendix I species may be traded commercially without restrictions
x: Appendix I generally prohibits commercial trade.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Appendix I — Corals and many sharks and rays
Appendix III — Walrus protected by Canada
Appendix I — Trade allowed merely with a certificate of origin
x: The walrus is an example associated with Appendix III, where Canada’s protection and request for cooperation are relevant. Tigers and rhinoceroses are Appendix I species, while corals and many sharks and rays are generally in Appendix II.

s: At CITES CoP20, in which Appendix were the whale shark, oceanic whitetip and manta rays listed?
x: Most sharks and rays are in Appendix II, but CoP20 listed the whale shark, oceanic whitetip and manta rays in Appendix I.
