s: CITES CoP20 at Samarkand was historically significant as which of the following?
o: First CITES COP held in Central Asia
First CITES COP held in Europe
First CITES COP held in Africa
First CITES COP held in South Asia
x: CITES CoP20 was the first CITES Conference of the Parties held in Central Asia.

s: How are species moved between CITES Appendices?
o: A vote of the Conference of the Parties
A decision of IUCN's Red List Committee
An automatic UNEP review every five years
An order of national wildlife authorities
x: Species move between CITES Appendices only through a vote of the Conference of the Parties.

s: In which year did India become a Party to CITES?
x: India became a Party to CITES in 1976. 1973 is the year CITES was adopted, 1975 the year it entered into force, and 1982 the year India joined the Ramsar Convention.

s: How often does the Conference of the Parties to CITES ordinarily meet?
x: The CITES COP meets every two to three years.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding CITES CoP3 is correct?
o: It was held in Panama in 2022 and added 54 sharks and rays to Appendix II.
It was held in Samarkand in 2025 and marked 50 years of CITES.
It was held in New Delhi in 1981 and remains the only CITES COP hosted by India.
It was held in New Delhi in 2019 and uplisted the Indian star tortoise.
x: CoP3 was held in New Delhi in 1981 and is the only CITES COP hosted by India.

s: At CoP20, India defeated a European Union proposal seeking a stricter CITES listing of which species?
x: At CoP20, India defeated the European Union proposal for a stricter listing of Guggul, scientifically known as Commiphora wightii.

s: Where was CITES CoP19 (2022), which added 54 sharks and rays to Appendix II, held?
x: CoP19 was held in Panama in 2022; the first CITES CoP in Central Asia was CoP20 at Samarkand in 2025.

s: When did CITES enter into force?
x: CITES was adopted on 3 March 1973 at Washington D.C. and entered into force on 1 July 1975.

s: Where is the CITES Secretariat, administered by UNEP, located?
x: The CITES Secretariat is at Geneva; Gland hosts the Ramsar Secretariat.

s: World Wildlife Day, observed on 3 March, marks the signing of which convention?
x: 3 March is the CITES signing day, proclaimed World Wildlife Day by the UNGA in 2013.

s: Under CITES, in which Appendix is a species listed that is not necessarily threatened but could become so without trade control?
x: Appendix II species may be traded with an export permit; Appendix I is for species threatened with extinction.

s: What is the full form of CITES?
o: Convention on International Treaty for Endangered Species
Conference on International Trade in Environmental Services
Convention on Intergovernmental Trade in Endangered Species
Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora
x: CITES is the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora, also called the Washington Convention.

s: Which of the following was among India's species proposals at CITES COPs?
x: India's CITES proposals include rosewood, otters, tortoises, the Tokay gecko and wedgefish.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its CITES Appendix?
x: Indian and Chinese pangolins are in Appendix I. The striped hyena is in Appendix II, rosewood (Dalbergia) is in Appendix II, and the AP-endemic golden gecko is in Appendix II, not III.

s: Who maintains the CITES Trade Database?
x: The CITES Trade Database is kept by UNEP-WCMC, not the Secretariat.

s: Under which Ministry does the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau, which enforces CITES, function?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: WCCB is a statutory body under MoEFCC.

s: Which programme monitors elephant poaching?
x: MIKE tracks elephant poaching; WCCB assists Customs and builds the wildlife-crime database.

s: For what was the new Schedule IV created by the Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022?
o: Specimens listed in the CITES Appendices
x: The amendment added a CITES chapter and Schedule IV for CITES-listed specimens; invasive alien species fall under a separate new section.

s: The golden gecko, endemic to Andhra Pradesh, is listed in which CITES Appendix?
x: The golden gecko is in Appendix II; tiger and clouded leopard are in Appendix I and red sanders in Appendix II.

s: In which year was the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau, a statutory body under MoEFCC, set up?
x: The WCCB was set up in 2007 through the 2006 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act.

s: When was India removed from the CITES Review of Significant Trade for red sanders?
x: India was under the Review of Significant Trade since 2004 and was removed at the 77th Standing Committee, Geneva, in November 2023.

s:
Consider the following statements about red sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus):
1. It is endemic to Seshachalam and the southern Eastern Ghats.
2. It is listed as Endangered by IUCN.
3. It is listed in CITES Appendix I.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; red sanders is in CITES Appendix II, not Appendix I.

s: Which organisation hosts a CITES Cell in India?
x: The Zoological Survey of India hosts a CITES Cell.

s: Which international agreement is also known as the 'Washington Convention'?
x: CITES was signed at Washington D.C. on 3 March 1973, hence 'Washington Convention'; 3 March is World Wildlife Day. CMS is the Bonn Convention.

s: Who was the first Indian to receive the Luc Hoffmann Award of IUCN?
x: Dhrubajyoti Ghosh got the award in 2016 for his work on the East Kolkata Wetlands.

s: Which of the following groups of species was added to CMS Appendix I at CMS COP-13 hosted by India?
o: Blue whale, dugong and olive ridley turtle
Ganges dolphin, snow leopard and blackbuck
Great Indian Bustard, Asian elephant and Bengal florican
Tiger, Asiatic lion and one-horned rhinoceros
x: The Great Indian Bustard, Asian elephant and Bengal florican were added to CMS Appendix I at COP-13.

s: By what other name is the Convention on Migratory Species known?
x: CMS is the Bonn Convention, a binding treaty under UNEP on conservation of migratory species.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: TRAFFIC — Wildlife trade should not threaten conservation
IUCN — Enforcement of CITES through customs inspections
CITES — Regulation of international wildlife trade
x: IUCN is associated with the Red List and field projects. Customs inspections for CITES consignments are assisted by the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau, while TRAFFIC is an NGO network concerned with wildlife trade.

s: Under the Bonn Convention (CMS), in which Appendix are endangered migratory species given strict protection listed?
x: CMS Appendix I lists endangered migratory species under strict protection; Appendix II lists species needing international cooperation agreements.

s: Which organisation, a union of governments and NGOs, maintains the Red List of threatened species?
x: IUCN is a union of governments and NGOs that maintains the Red List and runs field projects; it is not a UN organ.

s: TRAFFIC, which works to ensure wildlife trade is not a threat to conservation, is a network of which organisations?
x: TRAFFIC (1976) is an NGO network of WWF and IUCN, not a UNEP bureau.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the IUCN?
o: It is a union of governments and NGOs
It is an organ of the United Nations
x: IUCN is a union of governments and NGOs, not a UN organ.

s: Where was the 14th Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Migratory Species (CMS COP14) held in February 2024?
x: CMS COP14 was held at Samarkand, Uzbekistan, from 12 to 17 February 2024; India hosted COP13 at Gandhinagar in 2020.

s: What was the theme of CMS COP14 held at Samarkand in 2024?
x: CMS COP14 (2024) had the theme 'Nature knows no borders'; it was the first biodiversity COP after the Kunming-Montreal GBF.

s: Which city of Brazil is the venue of COP15 of the Convention on Migratory Species (CMS)?
x: CMS COP15 is at Campo Grande, Brazil, after COP14 at Samarkand (2024) and COP13 at Gandhinagar (2020).

s: In which year was the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) founded?
x: IUCN was founded in 1948; TRAFFIC, the WWF-IUCN network, came in 1976.

s: Rio+5, held in 1997, primarily involved which of the following?
o: A special session of the UN General Assembly reviewing Agenda 21
Establishment of the UNEA at Nairobi
x: Rio+5 was a special session of the United Nations General Assembly held in New York in 1997 to review the implementation of Agenda 21.

s: Which one of the following pairs of instruments was opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit, 1992?
x: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Convention on Biological Diversity were opened for signature at Rio in 1992.

s: Which of the following was an output of the Rio+20 Conference held in 2012?
o: The Montreal Protocol and Kyoto Protocol
Stockholm Declaration and creation of UNEP
The Future We Want and initiation of the SDG process
x: Rio+20, held in Rio de Janeiro in 2012, produced “The Future We Want”, launched the Sustainable Development Goal process and was associated with the High-Level Political Forum.

s: Agenda 21, an action plan for sustainable development at all levels, was an outcome of which conference?
o: The UN Conference on Environment and Development, 1992
The World Summit on Sustainable Development, 2002
The UN Conference on Sustainable Development, 2012
x: Agenda 21 came from UNCED, the 1992 Rio Earth Summit, the first international Earth Summit. Stockholm 1972 produced the Stockholm Declaration and UNEP, WSSD 2002 the Johannesburg Plan of Implementation, and Rio+20 'The Future We Want'.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rio Earth Summit, 1992 and its follow-ups?
o: The UNCCD was adopted in 1994 as a Rio follow-up
The UNFCCC, CBD and UNCCD are the three Rio Conventions
The Forest Principles adopted at Rio are a legally binding convention
The UNFCCC and the CBD were opened for signature at Rio
x: The Forest Principles were a non-binding statement, not a legally binding convention.

s: Along with UNDP and UNEP, which was an initial implementing partner of the Global Environment Facility?
x: GEF's first implementing partners were UNDP, UNEP and the World Bank; the CBD is a convention it funds.

s: Where was Rio+10, the World Summit on Sustainable Development of 2002, held?
x: Rio+10 (WSSD) was held at Johannesburg in 2002 and produced the Johannesburg Plan of Implementation.

s: The UN Environment Assembly (UNEA) was set up as an outcome of which conference?
x: UNEA came from Rio+20 (2012); UNEP came from Stockholm 1972, though both are in Nairobi.

s: When did the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) enter into force?
x: The UNFCCC, opened for signature at Rio 1992, entered into force on 21 March 1994.

s: In which year was the pilot Global Environment Facility (GEF) agreed?
x: The pilot GEF was agreed in 1990 and set up on the eve of the Rio Earth Summit, 1992.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Convention on Biological Diversity?
o: It was opened for signature at the Stockholm Conference, 1972
Its Secretariat is located in Montreal, Canada
It is one of the three Rio Conventions
Its financial mechanism is the Global Environment Facility
x: The CBD was opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in 1992, not at Stockholm in 1972.

s:
Assertion (A): In-situ conservation means conservation outside the natural habitat.
Reason (R): Ex-situ conservation means conservation outside the natural habitat.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false and R is true: in-situ conservation protects species in their natural habitat. Conservation outside the habitat is ex-situ.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: CBD COP11 was held at Hyderabad in 2012; COP10 was at Nagoya (2010), COP12 at Pyeongchang (2014) and COP13 at Cancun (2016).

s: Where was CBD COP16 held in 2024?
x: COP14 was at Sharm el-Sheikh (2018), COP15 at Kunming and Montreal (2021-22) and COP16 at Cali (2024).

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three objectives of the Convention on Biological Diversity?
o: Sustainable use of the components of biodiversity
Compulsory transfer of all genetic technologies to developing countries
Fair and equitable sharing of benefits from genetic resources
x: The CBD objectives are conservation, sustainable use and fair and equitable benefit-sharing. Compulsory transfer of all genetic technologies is not one of its objectives.

s: The Aichi Biodiversity Targets were adopted at which Conference of the Parties and in which year?
x: The 20 Aichi Biodiversity Targets were adopted at CBD COP10, held at Nagoya in 2010. COP12 at Pyeongchang reviewed their progress but did not adopt them.

s: When did the Convention on Biological Diversity enter into force?
x: The CBD text was adopted on 22 May 1992 and it entered into force on 29 December 1993.

s: In which year did India ratify the Convention on Biological Diversity?
x: India ratified the CBD in 1994; the Biological Diversity Act followed in 2002.

s: Which pair of CBD COP and venue is correctly matched?
x: COP14 was at Sharm el-Sheikh; COP10 was Nagoya, COP12 Pyeongchang and COP16 Cali.

s: Where was the first Conference of the Parties (COP1) to the Convention on Biological Diversity held in 1994?
x: CBD COP1 was held at Nassau, Bahamas, in 1994; COP13 was at Cancun in 2016.

s: Which of the following is a criticism directed at the Biological Diversity Amendment Act, 2023?
o: It transferred all biodiversity powers to the UNCCD
It completely abolished access and benefit-sharing mechanisms
It was criticised for diluting access and benefit-sharing and reducing the role of local communities
It prohibited the use of genetic resources for research
x: The amendment has been criticised for diluting access and benefit-sharing, increasing biopiracy risks and reducing the role of local communities.

s: By which year does the Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board aim to achieve zero loss of biodiversity and ecosystem services?
x: The AP State Biodiversity Board aims at zero loss of biodiversity and ecosystem services by 2050.

s: Under India's biodiversity framework, which bodies can levy collection fees for access to biological resources in their area?
x: BMCs can levy collection fees; the NBA at Chennai gives ABS approvals for foreign users.

s: Under India's three-tier biodiversity structure, who prepares People's Biodiversity Registers?
x: BMCs prepare People's Biodiversity Registers and can levy collection fees.

s: What is the name of the online biodiversity information portal launched by the Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board?
x: AP State Biodiversity Board runs the BIOMIS and ABS End-to-End portals; PRANA is CPCB's NCAP portal.

s: Where is the headquarters of the National Biodiversity Authority?
x: The National Biodiversity Authority is based in Chennai and gives ABS approvals for foreign users.

s: What does Goal C of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework concern?
o: Fair sharing of benefits from genetic resources
x: Goal C concerns fair sharing of benefits from genetic resources; finance and technology is Goal D.

s: How many Aichi Biodiversity Targets were set under the Strategic Plan 2011-2020?
x: There were 20 Aichi targets under five strategic goals; 23 is the number of KMGBF targets.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about biodiversity instruments?
o: The Cartagena Protocol concerns biosafety and living modified organisms
The Nagoya Protocol concerns access and benefit-sharing
The Kunming-Montreal GBF has four 2050 goals and 23 targets for 2030
x: The Aichi Targets numbered 20 for 2011-2020; 23 targets belong to the Kunming-Montreal GBF.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework?
o: It has four goals for 2050 and 23 targets for 2030
It was adopted at CBD COP16 at Cali in 2024
It seeks to halve food waste
x: The framework was adopted at COP-15 in December 2022 (Montreal), not at COP16.

s: Target 2 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework relates to which of the following?
o: Restoration of 30% of degraded land and water ecosystems
Conservation of 30% of land and oceans
Reducing harmful subsidies by US$500 billion annually
x: Target 2 calls for effective restoration of 30% of degraded land and water ecosystems by 2030. Conservation of 30% of land and oceans is Target 3.

s: Which target of the Kunming-Montreal GBF seeks to halve global food waste by 2030?
x: Target 16 seeks to halve food waste; Target 6 concerns invasive alien species.

s: By at least how much does Target 18 of the Kunming-Montreal GBF call for reducing harmful subsidies?
x: Target 18 calls for a reduction of harmful subsidies by at least US$500 billion a year.

s: Target 19 of the KMGBF seeks mobilisation of at least how much annually by 2030 from all sources?
x: Target 19 seeks at least US$200 billion per year by 2030 from all sources. This is the overall resource-mobilisation target, not the size of the GBF Fund itself.

s: How many national targets does India's updated National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan for 2024–2030 contain?
x: India’s updated NBSAP contains 23 national targets matching the 23 targets of the KMGBF.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Kunming-Montreal GBF is correctly matched?
o: Target 2 – Conserve 30% of land and 30% of oceans

Target 22 – Full participation and rights of indigenous peoples and local communities

s: The '30x30' target to conserve 30% of land and 30% of oceans by 2030 is part of which framework?
x: 30x30 is a biodiversity conservation target of the Kunming-Montreal GBF, not a renewable-energy target.

s: Where and when was the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework adopted?
x: The KMGBF was adopted at Montreal in December 2022, not at Kunming in 2021 or Cali in 2024.

s: How many targets and goals does the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework have?
x: The KMGBF has 23 targets for 2030 and 4 goals for 2050; Aichi had 20 targets under 5 strategic goals.

s:

1. They were adopted at CBD COP10 at Nagoya in 2010.
2. Their deadline was 2030.
3. Global Biodiversity Outlook 5 found none of them fully met.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; the Aichi deadline was 2020, while the KMGBF targets run to 2030.

s: By at least how much does Target 6 of the Kunming-Montreal GBF seek to cut the introduction and establishment of invasive alien species?
x: Target 6 seeks a cut of at least 50% in invasive alien species.

x: India joined on 7 October 2021 as the first BRICS country.

s: Which target of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework calls for halving excess nutrients and the risk from pesticides?
x: Target 7 seeks to halve excess nutrients and pesticide risk; Target 6 is on invasive species and Target 16 on food waste.

x: Goal A seeks to cut the extinction rate tenfold and halt human-induced extinction.

o: The first review of the Sendai Framework targets

s: At which COP did India release its updated National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2024-2030?
x: India's updated NBSAP with 23 national targets was released at COP16, Cali, in October 2024.

s: Under which Article of the Convention on Biological Diversity are national reports submitted?
x: National reports are submitted under Article 26, about every four years; Article 8(j) relates to indigenous peoples.
